blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) adapts a pretrained source model to unlabeled target domains without source data access, yet two critical failure modes remain unaddressed. First, attention drift: source-learned attention maps shift toward spurious or background features under distribution shift, destabilizing feature representations. Second, domain-gap-agnostic initialization: applying a single fixed source model uniformly across all target domains ignores domain gap severity, causing premature overfitting to noisy pseudo-labels under large shifts. We propose DGA-CAFC to address both failures. The Counterfactual Attention-based Feature Consistency (CAFC) module enforces feature stability by minimizing the discrepancy between representations computed under learned attention and those under counterfactual-inspired normalized perturbations, thereby promoting domain-robust features independent of spurious attention shifts. The Domain-Gap Aware Source Model Selection (DGASS) module estimates domain gap severity via target prediction entropy and selects the source model variant whose confidence level best matches the estimated gap, reducing negative transfer and stabilizing pseudo-label quality. Crucially, CAFC transfers beyond SFDA: applied as a lightweight regularizer to standard domain generalization objectives without target data. Extensive experiments across SFDA and DG benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently improves over recent baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness and generality of the proposed framework. Project page is available at https://visdomlab.github.io/DGA_CAFC

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Visual recognition models trained on a labelled source domain
degrade when deployed under distribution shift caused by
differences in imaging conditions, object appearance, texture,
background composition, or acquisition device.
Two settings address this without full re-annotation of the
target domain.
In source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) [ 14 , 30 , 29 , 12 ] ,
a source-trained model and unlabeled target data are available
at adaptation time, but the source training set is inaccessible
due to privacy or storage constraints.
In domain generalization (DG) [ 4 , 19 ] ,
no target data are available during training at all; the model
must generalize to unseen domains at test time.
Both settings demand representations that are stable under
covariate shift, yet the mechanisms by which standard
training produces fragile representations remain insufficiently
characterized.

blocks.en:
Transformer-based backbones [ 3 , 16 ] dominate visual recognition, including domain adaptive
models [ 27 , 21 ] .
Their self-attention mechanism aggregates features from all
spatial tokens, weighting each by a learned attention map
derived from source-domain statistics.
Under target-domain shift, these attention maps can drift
toward spurious or background features that are discriminative
in the source domain but not in the target,
a phenomenon we term attention drift .
Attention drift destabilizes the attention-conditioned
feature representations on which downstream tasks
depends: in SFDA, where a teacher model generates pseudo-labels
from these representations, corrupted features propagate
errors into the pseudo-label signal and compound through
self-training; in DG, drifted attention patterns reduce
robustness to the appearance variations encountered at test
time on unseen domains.
Despite the broad adoption of attention-based backbones, existing
SFDA and DG methods do not directly target the stability
of attention-conditioned features under distribution shift.
A second, SFDA-specific failure mode arises at initialisation.
Standard SFDA methods [ 14 , 27 ] initialise the student model from a single fixed source
checkpoint regardless of the severity of the domain gap
between source and target.
This is suboptimal because gap severity varies substantially
across transfer tasks: a high-gap pair requires a conservative
initialisation that does not over-commit to source-domain
decision boundaries, whereas a low-gap pair benefits from
a confident initialisation that accelerates pseudo-label
convergence.
Ignoring this distinction causes premature overfitting to
noisy pseudo-labels under large domain shifts, degrading
adaptation quality from the first training step.

blocks.en:
We propose DGA-CAFC , a two-module framework that
addresses both failure modes ( Fig. 2 ).
The Counterfactual Attention-based Feature Consistency ( CAFC ) module enforces stability in
attention-conditioned features by minimizing the discrepancy
between representations computed under the model’s learned
attention map and those computed under three
counterfactual-inspired normalised attention perturbations:
a uniform map that removes all focal structure, a random
map that injects noise, and a reversed map that inverts
saliency.
Minimising this discrepancy is analogous to Lipschitz-style
regularization in attention-conditioned feature space: it
reduces the sensitivity of the learned representation to the
specific attention weight configuration, encouraging
domain-robust features that do not depend on
source-specific attention patterns.
Critically, CAFC requires no target labels and operates
on attention outputs, making it directly applicable in both
SFDA and DG settings without architectural modification.
The Domain-Gap Aware Source Model Selection ( DGASS ) module addresses the SFDA initialisation
problem by estimating target domain gap severity from
unlabeled target prediction entropy and selecting the
source model variant between a sharp, confident variant
and a smoother, more conservative one.
Our contributions can be summarized as follows:

Pseudo-label refinement methods such as

blocks.en: 3.2 Framework Overview
blocks.zh: 3.2 框架概览

blocks.en:
DGA-CAFC addresses two distinct failure modes of SFDA
through two complementary modules ( Fig. 2 ). Attention drift , wherein source-learned attention maps
shift toward spurious target-domain features is addressed by CAFC ( Fig. 1 ) (Sec. 3.3 ), which regularises
attention-conditioned features throughout adaptation. Domain-gap-agnostic initialisation , wherein a single
fixed source model is applied uniformly regardless of domain gap
severity, it is addressed by DGASS (Sec. 3.4 ), which selects the source variant
best matched to the target domain’s estimated gap at
initialization time.
The two modules are architecturally independent: DGASS acts
once before training begins whereas CAFC acts at every gradient step.

blocks.en:
In the domain generalization (DG) setting, no target data
are available during training, making DGASS inapplicable.
We therefore apply ℒ CAFC \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CAFC}} alone as a
lightweight regularizer during source-domain training. The
same counterfactual attention perturbations and CAFC loss are
computed on source-domain batches without requiring target
data. Since the ResNet backbones used here do not natively produce transformer-style attention maps, we append a lightweight self-attention adapter: the 512-dimensional

before classification. We evaluate CAFC under two protocols: a ResNet-18-from-scratch isolation setting and a standard DomainBed-style setting with ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50. The former isolates the contribution of CAFC from ImageNet pretraining, while the latter enables direct comparison with standard DG evaluations.

SHOT, CoWA-JMDS, and NRC on the same ResNet-50+attention backbone used by
DGA-CAFC, using each method’s official code and published hyperparameters.
Only the same lightweight self-attention module is added, with no other
architectural or training changes. Compared with the original ResNet-50
results in Table 7 , adding attention alone degrades
all three baselines, most severely NRC ( − 7.04 -7.04 % on Office31 and − 8.14 -8.14 %

attention-conditioned features. On the identical backbone, DGA-CAFC
substantially outperforms all re-run baselines on both datasets, showing that
its gains cannot be attributed to the stronger backbone alone.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We presented DGA-CAFC, a source-free domain adaptation framework
designed to address two key limitations: attention drift under domain
shift and domain-gap agnostic source initialization. CAFC enforces
feature consistency under attention perturbations,
while DGASS selects a source model variant using target prediction
entropy to better match the estimated domain gap. Across Office31,
Office-Home, and DomainNet40, DGA-CAFC consistently improves SFDA
performance and calibration, with complementary gains from both
modules. CAFC also transfers to the DG setting, improving
standard DG objectives on PACS and VLCS without target data.
Results suggest that attention-stability regularization is a
useful principle for domain-robust recognition.

blocks.en:
Median as an ℓ 1 \ell_{1} -robust statistic. For any finite set of scalar values { x i } i = 1 n \{x_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n} , any median
minimizes the sum of absolute deviations [ 6 , 11 ] : median ⁡ ( { x i } ) ∈ arg ⁡ min ⁡ ∑ i = 1 n c ⁡ | x i − c | . \operatorname{median}(\{x_{i}\})\in\arg\min_{c}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|x_{i}-c|. In contrast, the arithmetic mean minimizes squared deviations and is
therefore more sensitive to extreme entropy values. This distinction is
important for cross-task entropy statistics, where transfer tasks can have
substantially different domain-gap severity. Using the median gives each
task equal rank-based influence and provides an outlier-resistant operating
point for separating relatively low-gap and high-gap transfers.

Distribution-free validity. The median does not require a parametric assumption about the shape of the
cross-task entropy distribution. This is appropriate for DGASS because the
threshold must be computed without target labels or target validation
accuracy. Parametric alternatives, such as fitting a Gaussian model or
choosing a distribution-specific percentile, would require estimating
additional distributional parameters from the same unlabeled entropy
statistics. The median rule avoids this extra modeling assumption while
remaining fully label-free.

blocks.en: 8 Design Rationale for Counterfactual Perturbations
blocks.zh: 8 反事实干扰设计理由

blocks.en:
The three perturbations in Eq. (4) are designed to target structurally
distinct failure modes of attention under distribution shift. Inspired by
counterfactual attention interventions used in prior attention-learning
work [ 18 , 31 ] , we use a small set of
complementary perturbations rather than searching over the full space of
possible attention corruptions. These perturbations stress-test different
forms of attention instability that can arise when source-learned attention
patterns are applied to shifted target domains.

在分配转移中,不同的失败关注模式。 灵感来自
在前期关注学习中使用的反事实关注干预
工作[18,31],我们使用一小组
互为补充的扰动,而不是搜索
可能的关注 腐败。 这些扰动压力测试不同

Uniform attention. A unif A_{\mathrm{unif}} represents the no-focal-structure limit: attention is
spread uniformly across tokens, testing whether the downstream feature is
overly dependent on a concentrated learned attention pattern.

在符号之间统一分布,测试下游特征是否
过度依赖一种集中的学习的注意力模式。

blocks.en:
Random attention. A rand A_{\mathrm{rand}} represents unstructured corruption: attention weights are
replaced with a random row-normalized distribution, testing robustness to
noisy or unreliable attention allocation.

随机专注. 朗德·A·马特尔姆{兰德}代表无结构腐败:注意权重是
替换为随机行常态分布,测试稳健度
吵闹或不可靠的注意力分配。

blocks.en:
Reversed attention. A rev A_{\mathrm{rev}} represents complementary saliency: high-attention regions
under the learned map are suppressed while lower-attention regions are
emphasized, testing whether the representation over-relies on source-salient
regions that may not transfer under domain shift.

反向关注。 a rev A_{\ mathrm{rev}} 代表了互补的显著性:高关注度地区
在所学地图下被压制,而注意较低的地区则被压制

blocks.en:
Together, these perturbations cover three qualitatively different regimes:
removing focal structure, injecting unstructured noise, and emphasizing
regions complementary to the learned attention. We do not claim that they
exhaust all possible attention corruptions or form an optimal perturbation
basis. Instead, they provide a compact and label-free set of attention-space
stress tests for regularizing attention-conditioned features.

blocks.en:
Analysis of how different source model variants, trained with distinct attention modules impact the overall adaptation performance. For fair analysis we exclude the CAFC and DGASS modules from the adaptation framework. We train three variants of source model and adapt it on target domain by simply leveraging self-labeling and information maximization loss. Variants are created by utilizing different attention softmax against each variant, on office-home.
Variant-1 is trained with standard softmax-based attention weights ( α i ​ j 1 \alpha_{ij}^{1} ), variant-2 is trained with a weighted softmax ( α i ​ j 2 \alpha_{ij}^{2} ) and variant-3 is trained with learnable weighted average of variant-1 and variant-2 ( α i ​ j 3 \alpha_{ij}^{3} ) as shown in main paper.
As reported in Table 9 , different variants shows its generalizable ability. We select the best two variant which is Variant-1 and Variant-3 in this case. Based on this study, we utilized these two variants across all datasets.

blocks.en: To assess whether the improvements introduced by CAFC are robust to random-seed variation, we perform paired significance analysis using matched seed-level runs under the standard DomainBed-style ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 protocol. For each DG objective, the baseline model and its corresponding CAFC-augmented variant are evaluated using the same random seed. We conduct the analysis over four objectives for which complete matched seed-level results are available on both PACS and VLCS: CORAL, ERM, GroupDRO, and Mixup. This gives 4 4 objectives × \times 3 3 seeds = 12 =12 matched seed-objective observations per dataset.

blocks.en: These paired seed-level results complement the mean ± \pm standard-deviation results reported in the main paper. In particular, the gains from CAFC are not driven by a single objective or an isolated random seed: CAFC improves 10/12 matched runs on PACS and 12/12 on VLCS, with statistically significant paired improvements on both benchmarks. This strengthens the evidence that the observed DG gains under the standard DomainBed protocol reflect a systematic effect of the CAFC regularizer rather than random seed variation.
blocks.zh: 这些对等的种子级结果补充了正文所报的平均值±\pm标准分级结果. 特别是,CAFC的收益并非由单一目标或孤立的随机种子驱动:CAFC在PACS上改进了10/12匹配跑道,在VLCS上则改进了12/12匹配跑道,在统计学上这两个基准上都有显著的对接改进. 这加强了以下证据:标准域标协议下观察到的DG增益反映了CAFC常态化的系统效应,而不是随机的种子变异.
